name: Rox
summary: Rox develops an AI-native revenue platform that uses autonomous agents across prospecting, account management, CRM updates, and renewals.
overview: Rox positions itself as a revenue operating system that layers AI agents on top of existing sales systems. TechCrunch reported in March 2026 that a new financing valued the company at $1.2 billion; Rox did not confirm the round or valuation.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: TechCrunch reported that a new financing valued Rox at $1.2 billion; the round size was not disclosed.

bull_case: A unified agent layer that improves pipeline execution across a company's existing stack could replace a fragmented collection of sales tools.
bear_case: Rox competes with entrenched CRM, revenue-intelligence, and AI-sales providers, while its latest valuation remains reported rather than company-confirmed.
latest_round: Reported 2025 financing: $1.2B valuation; round size undisclosed
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: An AI-native revenue operating system for automating sales workflows.
company: Rox deploys AI agents across revenue workflows, including account monitoring, prospect research, outreach, and CRM updates. The company positions the product as a layer above systems such as Salesforce and Zendesk rather than a single sales point tool.

TechCrunch reported that Rox closed a financing at a $1.2 billion valuation, with General Catalyst leading, but the company did not comment on the report. Rox had previously announced $50 million of seed and Series A funding and named Ramp, MongoDB, and New Relic as customers.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Revenue operations is a concrete commercial test for autonomous agents: the buyer wants measurable productivity, not generic AI experimentation. Rox is an indicator of how much private capital is underwriting that workflow shift.

changed.text: TechCrunch reported a new financing at a $1.2B valuation; Rox did not confirm it.

takeaways: The $1.2B valuation is reported and not company-confirmed.
The thesis depends on measurable sales-workflow automation and account expansion.
CRM incumbents and new AI-native rivals remain strong competitive constraints.
